title: fix(cli): os serve refuses an OS_DATABASE_URL whose scheme no driver recognises, and reads pg:// and a scheme-less path as the runtime host does
body:
Fixes #23633
Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`inferDriverTypeFromUrl` (`packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts`) is how `os serve` classifies `OS_DATABASE_URL` on its legacy path. A host config takes that path (one whose `plugins` hold plugin instances), and so does `OS_MODE=off|none|legacy`. `os dev` and `os start` reach it through their `serve` child. The function answered `''` for any URL its regexes missed.

- **An unrecognised `SCHEME://` (`redis://…`) is now refused.** The function throws `UnsupportedDriverError` (`recognized: false`), as it already does for `memory://` and `mingo://`. The message names `OS_DATABASE_URL`, the scheme, and the recognised spellings in the runtime host's order. It names the scheme only, never the URL, so credentials in the URL are not printed. serve.ts calls `resolveDriverType` above its storage `try`, so the throw reaches the fatal handler and the boot exits 1 in dev and production. serve.ts is not edited.
- **The runtime host's arms are adopted.** `pg://` is postgres, and a value with no `SCHEME://` is a SQLite file path, whatever its extension. Both match `detectDriverFromUrl` (`packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts`, read only) character for character. The runtime host refuses every other `SCHEME://`, so the CLI host refuses nothing the runtime host accepts.
- **A `.db` ending no longer rescues an unrecognised scheme.** The old `*.db` arm ran before any scheme check, so `redis://h/app.db` was handed to SQLite as a file path. It is now refused, as the runtime host refuses it.
- **A blank URL is absent.** Whitespace-only values still answer `''`. Without that guard the new scheme-less arm would read them as a file path.
- An explicit `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER` still wins. `resolveDriverType` does not classify the URL at all when a driver is named.

The `memory://` / `mingo://` refusal and every recognised spelling resolve exactly as before. No export is added, and `packages/spec` is not touched.

## Measured at the public door

Built CLI (`node packages/cli/bin/run.js`), `NODE_ENV` unset, `OS_CLOUD_URL=off`, auth secret set. The fixture is a throwaway `defineStack` host config: one object and one instantiated no-op plugin. Before = base `3b46855fb`; after = this branch at `54933125a`, built.

| Shape | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `OS_DATABASE_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6399/0 os serve --dev` | `✓ Server is ready`, banner `Driver: SqlDriver(better-sqlite3) → :memory:` | exit 1, `✗ Unsupported database URL scheme "redis://" (OS_DATABASE_URL / --database). Supported: …` |
| the same, production (`os serve`) | exit 1, the no-storage refusal ("set OS_DATABASE_URL …") | exit 1, the same unsupported-scheme line |
| `os dev --no-watch`, same URL | `🗄️ Database: redis://127.0.0.1:6399/0`, then the banner `→ :memory:` | exit 1, the unsupported-scheme line |
| `os start`, same URL | exit 1, the no-storage refusal | exit 1, the unsupported-scheme line |
| `redis://admin:PASSWORD@127.0.0.1:6399/0 os serve --dev` | banner `→ :memory:` | exit 1; the password occurs 0 times in the output |
| `pg://u:p@127.0.0.1:5999/db`, `--dev` | banner `→ :memory:` | exit 1, `datasource 'default': connect failed — connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5999` (the URL is used) |
| the same, production | exit 1, the no-storage refusal | exit 1, the same connect failure |
| `./data/app`, `--dev` | banner `→ :memory:` | `✓ Server is ready`, banner `→ ./data/app`; the file exists |
| `./data/app2`, production | exit 1, the no-storage refusal | `✓ Server is ready`, banner `→ ./data/app2` |
| CONTROL `memory://`, `--dev` | exit 1, the retirement sentence | unchanged |
| CONTROL `postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:5999/db`, `--dev` | exit 1, connect ECONNREFUSED | unchanged |
| CONTROL `file:./ctl.db`, production | `✓ Server is ready`, `→ file:./ctl.db` | unchanged |
| CONTROL `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=postgres` + `redis://127.0.0.1:6399/0`, `--dev` | (not measured before) | exit 1, connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6399: the explicit driver wins and the scheme is not refused |
| a plain config (runtime host), `redis://…`, `--dev` | exit 1, `[StandaloneStack] Unsupported database URL scheme: …` | unchanged (not this path) |

## The two hosts, URL by URL

The runtime host's verdict is `resolveStandaloneDatabase` from `@objectstack/runtime`. The CLI host's is `resolveStorageDefinition(resolveDriverType(undefined, url), …)`. Only the rows that moved are listed; every other row (`postgres://`, `postgresql://`, `mysql://`, `mysql2://`, `mongodb://`, `mongodb+srv://`, `libsql://`, `https://*.turso.io`, `wasm-sqlite://`, `*.wasm.db`, `memory://`, `mingo://`, `file:`, `sqlite:`, `sqlite://`, `:memory:`, `*.db`, `*.sqlite`, `*.sqlite3`) was already equal and is unchanged.

| `OS_DATABASE_URL` | CLI before (dev / prod) | CLI after (dev / prod) | runtime host |
|---|---|---|---|
| `redis://…`, `REDIS://…`, `rediss://…`, `http(s)://` (not turso), `ftp://`, `mssql://`, `sqlserver://`, `oracle://`, `cockroachdb://`, `mariadb://` | `:memory:` default / `null` | refused / refused | refused |
| `pg://…`, `PG://…` | `:memory:` default / `null` | postgres / postgres | postgres |
| `./data/app`, `/tmp/…/app`, `app`, `C:\data\app`, `C:/data/app` | `:memory:` default / `null` | sqlite / sqlite | sqlite |
| `jdbc:postgresql://h/db`, `redis:h` (a scheme with no `//`) | `:memory:` default / `null` | sqlite / sqlite | sqlite (see the finding below) |

## Pins

All under `packages/cli/src/**`, in the unit tier.

- `utils/storage-driver.test.ts`:
  - `pg://` / `PG://` map to postgres, and four scheme-less paths map to sqlite;
  - `''` comes back only for an absent or blank URL;
  - five refused URLs, `redis://h/app.db` among them, each checked for the error type, `recognized: false`, `driverType` = the scheme, and that the message names `OS_DATABASE_URL`, the scheme and the recognised spellings;
  - the refusal does not carry the URL's credentials or host;
  - an explicit driver still wins over an unrecognised scheme.
  - The old row asserting `inferDriverTypeFromUrl('redis://localhost') === ''` pinned the defect. It is replaced.
- `utils/driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts`, a new block, "the OS_DATABASE_URL door", driving both hosts:
  - 19 URLs that the runtime host accepts. Each is accepted by both hosts as the same kind, and the CLI builds its definition from that URL (`displayUrl === url`) in dev and in prod. A bare driver-id check would read the dev `:memory:` default as agreement.
  - 5 URLs that both hosts refuse, in dev and in prod. The CLI's refusal is the typed one.
  - 2 opaque-scheme values on which the two hosts must give the same verdict, so a change to either host's scheme-less arm reds until the other follows.

**Not landed: a real-boot pin.** The fixture that spawns the built `bin/run.js` in production posture lives under `packages/cli/test/`. A new spawner there also joins the built-entrypoint roster in `scripts/check-cli-test-child-env.mjs`. Both are outside this card's file surface. The CLI's existing refusals (`memory://`, unknown `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER`) are pinned at this same unit layer in both modes. The boots above are the one-off proof of the exit path.

## Ablation (one per behaviour changed; WRAP mode of `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, on-disk proof, restore proven as blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`)

| Leg | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | `return ''` restored for an unrecognised `SCHEME://` | 12 red / 117 green |
| A2 | `pg` dropped from the postgres arm | 3 red |
| A3 | the old `*.db` / `:memory:` arm in place of the scheme-less arm | 8 red, `redis://h/app.db` among them |
| A4 | the blank-URL guard removed | 1 red |

The first A1 attempt was a no-op: the tool refused it because the anchor was contained in the replacement, and restored the file. It was re-run with a non-overlapping replacement; the counts above are from that run.

## Tests and gates (head `683bf9587`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`: 295 files, 4399 tests passed. The diff touches no integration-tier file, spawn entry or driver/kernel boot path, so the `integration` layer is declared to CI.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0. `tsc --noEmit` covers `src/**` tests, then `check:test-typecheck` ran OK.
- `pnpm exec eslint packages/cli --no-inline-config`: exit 0, 696 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 64 commands, run in order, each exit captured before any pipe. 62 exited 0. 2 exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`) and are **NOT MEASURED**: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage`. Both read the built output of the whole workspace, and this local run built only the `@objectstack/cli` closure. CI runs both. `--ran` reconciliation: 64 derived, 62 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. The derivation read a tree 3 commits behind `origin/main`. The one derived-from file that moved there is `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json` (an objectui pin bump).

## Acceptance notes

- `serve.ts`'s step-2 comment block lists the URL-scheme priority. It now omits `pg://`, the scheme-less arm and the unrecognised-scheme refusal. It is not false, only incomplete. `serve.ts` is held by #23623 and is not edited here. Carrier: none.
- The no-storage refusal's phrase "no recognized OS_DATABASE_URL" (`serve.ts`) is now redundant rather than false: a URL that is set and unrecognised no longer reaches it.
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:522` says `os start` "auto-detects the driver from the database URL scheme (… otherwise sqlite …)". The runtime host already refused an unrecognised scheme before this change, and this change does not make the sentence false. No docs sentence is made false here, so no docs edit is made. Carrier: none.
- Mechanism hypothesis H3 is partly false. `os start` over a HOST config does reach this path, through its production `serve` child (measured above). Over a plain config, `os start` goes through the runtime host, as H3 said.

## Found while measuring, for the seat to file (not fixed here)

1. **The runtime host prints a refused URL's credentials.** class a · reach: measured at `os dev --no-watch` over a plain config with `OS_DATABASE_URL=redis://admin:PASSWORD@127.0.0.1:6399/0`. Its `🗄️ Database:` row redacts the credentials, then the refusal `[StandaloneStack] Unsupported database URL scheme: redis://admin:PASSWORD@…` prints them in full. Also exception: security. The landing is `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts` (`detectDriverFromUrl`'s throw). Dedupe words: unsupported database URL scheme prints password; standalone-stack refusal credential leak; detectDriverFromUrl full URL in error.
2. **The CLI host opens `sqlite://x.db` at the filesystem root.** class a · reach: measured with `OS_DATABASE_URL=sqlite://os23633-probe.db os serve --dev` over a host config. The banner read `→ sqlite://os23633-probe.db`, and the database was written to `/os23633-probe.db`. The runtime host normalises the same URL to `file:` and opens `./os23633-probe.db`. The cause is `resolveStorageDefinition`'s sqlite arm, which strips `sqlite:` and leaves `//x.db`. Dedupe words: sqlite:// double slash absolute path; CLI sqlite alias not normalised to file:; resolveStorageDefinition sqlite filename root.
3. **A value carrying a scheme with no `//` becomes a SQLite file on both hosts.** class a · reach: measured with `OS_DATABASE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5999/db os serve --dev` over a plain config (runtime host). It printed `✓ Server is ready`, `→ jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5999/db`, and created `./jdbc:postgresql:/127.0.0.1:5999/db`. The runtime host's own header says an unknown scheme never falls back to SQLite. Its scheme-less test only asks whether `SCHEME://` is present. The CLI host mirrors it by this card's ruling (it never refuses what the runtime host accepts), and the new parity row holds the two together. The fix is on both hosts at once. Dedupe words: jdbc URL treated as sqlite file; opaque scheme bare path arm; detectDriverFromUrl bogus directory.
